name: Port Plastics
old_description: Port Plastics delivers industrial plastic materials and custom fabrication services to manufacturers nationwide through 11 strategically located facilities.
about:
Port Plastics was founded in 1960 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a regional supplier of industrial plastic materials to local manufacturers. Over six decades, the company has grown into a national distributor with 11 strategically located facilities across the United States.

The company stocks more than 1,000 grades of high-performance engineering plastics — including PEEK, PTFE, polycarbonate, and acrylic — and operates in-house fabrication shops equipped with precision CNC machining centers, CNC routers, and panel saws capable of cutting material up to 5 inches thick and 11 feet long. Its fabrication services cover CNC machining to tolerances of ±0.001 inch, routing, drilling, thermoforming, and welding, supporting orders from prototype quantities to production runs. Same-day cutting and next-day delivery are available from its distributed inventory network.

Port Plastics serves semiconductor manufacturers requiring ultra-high-purity, FM4910-compliant materials for cleanroom environments; energy and oil-and-gas clients specifying NORSOK M-710-qualified components for subsea applications; aerospace and defense contractors relying on AS9100D-compliant quality systems and ITAR-registered facilities; medical and life-science companies needing USP Class VI biocompatible polymers; and food-and-beverage processors using FDA- and NSF-compliant materials for direct food contact.

The company positions itself as a technical partner rather than a pure material supplier, emphasizing its team of materials engineers who average 15-plus years of industry experience. It maintains deep inventory positions to buffer supply disruptions, provides full traceability documentation with every shipment, and holds ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, and ITAR registrations across its quality system.

name: Portland Bottling Company
old_description: For the most trusted, safest and highest quality ready-to-drink beverages in the industry, Portland Bottling Company is ready to deliver.
about:
Portland Bottling Company, founded in 1924, is headquartered in Clackamas, Oregon. The company has operated in the Pacific Northwest for nearly a century, establishing itself as a beverage co-packer. No founders are named in the source material, and ownership structure is not specified.

The company provides end-to-end co-packing services for ready-to-drink beverages in aluminum cans, including filling, secondary packaging, and warehousing. Its 500,000-square-foot footprint spans multiple facilities, with a state-of-the-art canning line capable of running up to 1,450 cans per minute. Processes cover cold fill, tunnel pasteurization, liquid nitrogen dosing, reverse-osmosis water treatment, and a range of can sizes from 8.4 oz to 16 oz. Automated cartoning handles 4‑ to 24‑pack configurations, variety packs, and registered film shrink wrap. On-site quality assurance labs and inline monitoring support FSSC 22000, HACCP, organic, gluten‑free, and kosher certifications.

Portland Bottling serves both national and independent beverage brands across the Western United States and Canada. Its customer base includes producers of carbonated juices, sparkling waters, energy drinks, functional beverages, coffee, tea, and carbonated sodas, with specialty certifications for organic, kosher, and gluten‑free products.

The company emphasizes proactive partnership, 24/7 production availability, and treating customer resources as its own. Its mission is to deliver the most trusted, safest, and highest‑quality RTD solutions while fostering a collaborative, family‑oriented workplace culture.

name: Portland Garment Factory
old_description: Portland Garment Factory (PGF) is a dynamic hub of creativity and innovation, working alongside daring designers, brands, agencies, and artists to create extraordinary fabric-based wonders, from custom creations to streamlined cut-and-sew productions.
about:
Portland Garment Factory (PGF) was founded in 2008 in Portland, Oregon, by Britt Howard. The woman-owned studio began as a zero-waste creative design and fabrication shop aiming to upend the traditional factory model through ethical labor practices and environmental sustainability.

The company provides full-service soft-goods manufacturing, including custom cut-and-sew production (20,000+ units), art fabrication, product development, prototyping, and retail/experiential fabrication. Operations run in-house with a team of 11–50 employees, supported by an internal experimentation lab (PGF Lab) for material and process innovation.

PGF serves designers, brands, agencies, and artists across apparel, retail, experiential marketing, art institutions, corporate branding, food and beverage, sports, technology, and hospitality. Clients have included Nike, Adidas, Intel, Portland Art Museum, Tillamook, Xbox, Converse, UGG, and DiGiorno, among others.

The studio’s differentiation rests on its zero-waste commitment, B Corporation certification, WBENC woman-owned certification, and Sustainability at Work Gold certification. Core values—Be Human, Think Forward, Honor Process, Respect Time, Invite Challenge—guide a model that blends creative ideation with responsible production.

name: Potter Webster Company
old_description: Locally owned and nationally known, Potter Webster is proud to be your parts supplier and we strive every day to be the best at what we do. As a family owned business since 1940, we have worked hard to bring quality parts and service to our industry. With the support of our loyal customers, we now house over 120 product lines in our 51,000 square ft Portland warehouse; this means we’ll have the parts you need when you need them. about:
Potter Webster Company has operated from Portland, Oregon since 1940 as a family-owned business. The company began as a local parts supplier and has grown into a nationally recognized distributor while remaining under family ownership.

The company stocks more than 120 product lines across a 51,000-square-foot warehouse, supplying components for commercial trucks and trailers. In addition to distribution, Potter Webster runs a service shop that performs light trailer repairs, machine-shop work, U-bolt bending, custom cable fabrication, fan-clutch rebuilding, and brake-shoe relining. The facility also supports hydraulic and PTO services, driveline work, and axle-system assembly.

Customers include fleet operators, repair shops, and dealers serving the heavy-duty transportation sector. The inventory features brands such as Hendrickson trailer-axle parts, Dana/Spicer drivetrain components, and Denso starters and alternators under the Power Edge label. Past acquisitions — including the assets of R.W. Conroy Company and Customer Parts & Trailer Supply — expanded the product range and led to the Custom Trailer Parts line.

The company states its mission is to keep vehicles safely on the road and profitable for their owners. A focus on value and on understanding customer needs has guided its evolution from a single location to a multi-line supplier with in-house service capabilities.

about:
Power Brace Manufacturing operates from Des Moines, Iowa, where it was founded in 2002. The company remains privately held; no founders are named in public materials. It began as a steel component manufacturer focused on defect-free delivery and continuous improvement.

The shop produces steel components through a range of in-house processes: CNC machining (centers up to 55 inches long), fiber laser tube cutting (6-axis, 3,000-watt, up to 6-inch OD, 21-foot length), fiber laser table cutting (4,000-watt, up to 1-inch thick, 5x10 feet), six robotic welding cells (12x3-foot work zones), automated zinc electroplating per ASTM B633 (tanks up to 12x5x17 feet), press brake forming (70- to 250-ton, up to 10-foot wide), HD plasma cutting with beveling up to 45 degrees (1.5-inch thick, 6x26 feet), and kitting/assembly/packaging. The facility is ISO 9001:2015 certified and emphasizes lean manufacturing.

Primary industries served include telecommunications, construction, transportation, defense, and agriculture. The company cites work with Verizon, AT&T, and Google, alongside smaller manufacturers, and ships throughout North America from Canada to Mexico.

Power Brace traces its differentiation to a "whatever it takes" work ethic, end-to-end solutions from raw material to packaged assembly, and a commitment to on-time, defect-free delivery through continuous improvement.

old_description: As a world-class manufacturer of Micro-Speed® variable frequency drives and Smooth-Move® reduced torque control units, PE® equipment is world-renowned for high reliability and quality. Multi-Vector® drives also make PE® the world leader in heavy-duty closed-loop quality hoist speed control. about:
Power Electronics International, Inc. (PE) operates from East Dundee, Illinois, where it designs, engineers, and manufactures its full line of motion control products for overhead cranes and hoists. The company focuses exclusively on crane and hoist applications, developing drives, soft-starts, and control systems tailored to those demands.

The product range includes Micro-Speed® variable frequency drives, Smooth-Move® reduced torque control units, Multi-Vector® closed-loop hoist drives, and a variety of control panels such as travel motion, hoist, multiple-motion, and custom configurations. PE also manufactures regeneration resistors for dynamic braking, the PE-SAM™ sensorless anti-swing system integrated into its Ultra Series drives, PE360™ rotation control for hook positioning, PLC-based automation for lifting systems, and the PE Mobi-Power™ wireless power system for mobile equipment. The company states that over a quarter of a million crane and hoist motions worldwide utilize its equipment.

PE serves overhead crane and hoist technicians, mechanics, and industrial material handling operations. Its products are specified for bridge cranes, trolley systems, monorails, gantry cranes, and tower cranes, and are integrated into custom control panels built to exact specifications for each installation.

The company emphasizes an Upgrade-Path™ philosophy, ensuring that all past and present programming methods remain compatible with future drive models. All hardware is designed, engineered, and manufactured in its East Dundee facility, and its control panels and automation systems carry UL and cUL approval.

name: Power Engineering and Manufacturing, Ltd.
old_description: Power Engineering & Manufacturing specializes in the custom design and manufacturing of heavy-duty gearboxes.
about:
Power Engineering & Manufacturing, Ltd. (PEM) was founded in 1975 in Waterloo, Iowa, by Saul Herscovici and several members of the Warren family. The company specializes in the custom design and manufacturing of heavy-duty gearboxes and has operated continuously from its Iowa headquarters for nearly five decades.

PEM provides complete gearbox solutions including design, manufacturing, reverse engineering, rebuild, and inspection services. Its machining capabilities encompass 12 CNC lathes, five CNC milling machines, two Okuma MCR-A5CII double-column machining centers, six CNC hobbing machines, five gear grinding machines, and additional grinding, shaping, keyseating, plasma cutting, sawing, dynamic balancing, robotic welding, and stress-relieving equipment. The facility also houses two large-capacity coordinate measuring machines for inspection.

The company serves customers in defense, aerospace, mining, and general industrial markets. Notable projects include AD-43 gearboxes for the U.S. Navy and units for helicopter test stands and roll crushers. PEM also repairs and rebuilds gearboxes from manufacturers such as Falk, Demag, Flender, and Dodge, and supports clients across the United States and in more than 48 countries.

PEM emphasizes ingenuity, attention to detail, and customer service as differentiators. Its proprietary MEGAGEAR® design can increase horsepower or torque by up to 35% over OEM designs, and the company offers expedited service and storage agreements to minimize downtime. Quality is managed under an ISO 9001:2015 certified system, and welding procedures are qualified to AWS D1.1, D1.5, D1.6, and NAVSEA standards.

name: Precise Cable Inc
old_description: Founded with the strongest work ethic we continue to communicate with honesty and fairness to all interested parties.
about:
Precise Cable Inc was founded in 1988 by Billie Van Ark in Longmont, Colorado. The company began as a home-based business driven by Van Ark's passion for providing fabrication solutions. Over three decades, it has grown from grassroots research into a global supplier of custom cable and wire harnessing products.

Today, Precise Cable operates a 15,000-square-foot facility near Denver and Boulder. The shop specializes in custom cable harnessing and precision electro-mechanical assemblies, offering both turnkey and contract manufacturing services. For projects requiring controlled environments, the company maintains ISO-certified clean rooms for fabrication.

The company serves a broad range of industries, including aerospace (flight and ground support), defense, government, commercial, medical, oil and gas, communications, instrumentation, agriculture, automotive, and test and measurement. Customers range from large aerospace programs to smaller commercial projects.

Precise Cable emphasizes that its people are the key differentiator, citing an experienced management team and talented personnel who compete on complex programs of all sizes. The business has grown largely through word-of-mouth referrals, reflecting a commitment to exceeding customer expectations and continuous improvement.

name: Precise Circuit Co
old_description: Precise Circuit Company has been providing high quality printed circuit board and electro-mechanical assembly services since 1985. Working closely with manufacturers we provide completed products, on time and at competitive cost.
about:
Precise Circuit Company, Inc. was founded in 1985 in Shelton, Connecticut, by Thomas Misencik Sr. after he completed electronic training at the Connecticut School of Electronics and small business management courses at Southern Connecticut State University. The company operates from a downtown Shelton location with easy access to Route 8. It is owned and managed by the Misencik family, with Tom Misencik Sr. serving as president and Tom Misencik Jr. also an owner.

The company provides printed circuit board assembly and electro-mechanical assembly services, specializing in surface-mount, through-hole, and mixed-technology processes. Its capabilities include prototype and production volumes, automated pick-and-place lines (two Samsung SM482 machines), stencil printing, reflow soldering (three Heller ovens), wave soldering (both leaded and lead-free), automatic optical inspection (Mirtec MV-3L), functional testing, and final box-build assembly. The facility also houses through-hole insertion equipment, a climate-controlled board storage room, and depaneling and cleaning systems.

Precise Circuit serves small to mid-sized original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across various industries, working directly with manufacturers to deliver completed electronic assemblies. The company emphasizes direct owner involvement and long-term customer relationships, though specific industry verticals are not publicly listed.

The company was started to provide quality electronic assemblies for smaller OEMs that needed responsive, transparent manufacturing partners. According to the founders, the “Precise Difference” lies in working directly with the owners, continuous customer interaction for manufacturing feedback, and a commitment to quality, transparency, and commitment at the lowest cost.
